newsitem.title: UK: NatWest Euro equity derivatives head quits.
newsitem.headline: NatWest Euro equity derivatives head quits.

text.p: NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc, said on Friday that its European equity derivatives head had left to join U.S. investment bank Lehman Brothers.

"Roger Nagioff has resigned to go to Lehman Brothers," a NatWest spokeswoman told Reuters. His departure is not connected to recent revelations of a 90 million stg loss in interest rate options at NatWest Markets.

NatWest hit the headlines on Thursday when it announced the results of a preliminary inquiry into the losses and the suspension of four senior employees. It also cut 8.0 million stg in bonuses for a handful of staff in its global debt derivatives division.

The bank also said that NatWest Market's chief executive Martin Owen would forgo 200,000 of a 500,000 stg bonus for 1996. The suspensions of five NatWest staff in all have also been passed to financial markets watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA).

And earlier on Friday it announced a major shake-up of its global debt markets wing, including the departure of two senior NatWest employees, Johan Hattingh, who was head of European fixed income, and Alby Cator, managing director of European primary markets.
